The transition length decreases as the turbulent spot production rate increases.
Much of the data used to develop transition length correlations was obtained at low Mach number, incompressible flow conditions.
Recent experimental data showed that the turbulent spot parameters are affected by Mach number, even at Mach numbers less than 1.

The paper used the turbulent spot data of Clark (1993) and the Tollmien-Schlichting wave frequency analysis of Mack (1969) to derive modifications to account for Mach number effects in the transition length models.
The modified transition length models were incorporated into the RVCQ3D Navier-Stokes code for comparison with experimental turbomachinery data.
For the stator cases examined, the Mach number at the start of transition ranged from 0.78 to 0.97.
For the rotor cases, the exit Mach numbers ranged from 0.8 to 1.3, with the start of transition occurring at Mach numbers up to 1.1.
Accounting for Mach number effects significantly improved the agreement between predicted and measured midspan surface heat transfer for both stator and rotor turbine blades.
The paper found that accurately predicting the start and length of transition is crucial for accurately predicting turbine blade heat transfer, especially in the absence of film cooling.
The Smith and Kuethe (1966) model was used to account for the effects of freestream turbulence on the laminar flow region.
